fields.acceptance: A testscript with fixture journals of a run blocked on a question, a run waiting at sign-off, a failed run, a run interrupted again after a daemon resume and a done run lists exactly the first four in order in text and --json; once the question is answered, the sign-off approved and the failed and given-up runs abandoned, rhiza inbox says nothing waits.
fields.statement: rhiza inbox lists, oldest first across every run of the repo, each item waiting on the owner with a short item ID: a question (its run, change set, session tab and the question), a run waiting at sign-off, a failed run (its failed step and detail, until it is resumed or abandoned), and a run the daemon gave up on (interrupted again after the daemon's one resume, its step, until it is resumed or abandoned), in text and --json, and says so when nothing waits.

fields.acceptance: A testscript with a fake Rex opens a question item and sees the asking session's tab focused, opens a sign-off item and sees the run's tab focused, and gets exit 2 for an unknown item.
fields.statement: rhiza inbox open <item> focuses the Rex tab of the session that asked a question, or of the run for a sign-off, a failed run or a run the daemon gave up on, so the owner answers in the agent's own menu; an unknown item exits 2.

fields.acceptance: With a fake Rex, a run that blocks on a question, then waits at sign-off, another that fails and a third the daemon gives up on send exactly four notifications, one per item, and none while each item stays in the inbox.
fields.statement: Each new inbox item sends one Rex notification naming the change set and what waits (a question, a sign-off, a failed run or a run the daemon gave up on), through the blocked-run notice path, and none again while the item stays.

This change set's intent still reads 'Genesis watches runs and passes their questions to the owner, with a recommendation drawn from slice and why', but answers 4, 7 and 16 made it the whole inbox: sign-offs approved or sent back, failed runs and runs the daemon gave up on, and a notification for each. No rhiza command restates a change set's intent. Should the intent be restated (which needs a way to do it), or should the sign-off and failed-run leaves move to a new change set whose intent covers them?
